evidence: src/application/services/OrderLookupService.ts: OrderLookupService.getById calls this.orders.findById (OrderRepository) and throws new NotFoundError('Order', orderId) when nothing is found.

src/application/services/StockAllocationService.ts: StockAllocationService.load calls this.products.findById (ProductRepository), throws new NotFoundError('Product', productId) when nothing is found, and returns the domain StockAllocation type.

src/application/services/StockAllocationService.ts: persist only calls this.products.save, so persistence stays behind the repository port. The ProductQuantity interface is an input DTO local to this service.
Graph: both services are constructor-injected into order use cases (CancelOrderUseCase, ShipOrderUseCase, PlaceOrderUseCase, etc.), so they act as shared use-case support services.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: Both files are application-layer helper services that use cases inject to load aggregates through domain repository ports. Each one throws the shared domain NotFoundError when an aggregate is missing. OrderLookupService loads orders. StockAllocationService loads products into StockAllocation pairs and saves them after stock moves. They have one concern: retrieving and persisting aggregates for use cases through repository abstractions. Neither bypasses the repositories. Both use the domain's NotFoundError and StockAllocation types instead of defining their own versions. The find-or-throw check appears in both files, but for different aggregates (Order and Product), each through its own repository. It is a small, shared idiom, not a business rule or invariant that should live in only one place. No stock or order rule is copied here: reservation logic stays in the domain StockReservationService. The module is cohesive and uses its abstractions consistently.
